newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Securities firm starts Ukraine stock index.
newsitem.headline: Securities firm starts Ukraine stock index.

text.p: Prague-based securities firm Wood and Company on Tuesday issued an index for Ukraine's embryonic shares market which will track the top 15 companies listed on the OTC stock trading system, the manager of its Kiev office said.
"With the recent privatisation of Ukraine's utilities and metallurgical companies, the essential blue chips have reached the market," Tomas Fiala said in a statement.
"We therefore feel a solid enough foundation has been established to calculate a benchmark for investors," he added.
The Wood15 Index, is based on June 13 at 1000.
The index is based on standards of the International Finance Corporation, the private-sector arm of the World Bank, which is expected to produce a larger index for Ukrainian shares by year's end.

There are several equities markets apart from the Kyiv PFTS OTC Stock Trading System, including the Ukrainian Stock Exchange, the Kyiv International Stock Exchange, and the Donetsk Stock Exchange. All are often characterised by thin trading and illiquidity.

U.S. firm Ladenburg Thalmann International Ltd. plans to start an index of top 50 Ukrainian companies by September, and Russian bank Alfa Capital also recently started tracking the OTC market with its AC-20 index.
